transcript.text: I need to share a confidential student-safety matter that directly impacts our election procedures. My confidential student-safety review found a substantiated retaliation concern involving two students in the election. Because of this, our student-privacy protocol requires anonymous voting and prohibits releasing vote totals until the election is certified. I've kept the review in my counseling file since it contains protected student information, and I had not yet briefed Dr. Morgan on this. What this means for our draft plan is that the online ballot must guarantee fully anonymous voting — not just private, but anonymous — and we cannot publish vote totals at the end of election day as currently planned. We would need to wait until the election is certified before releasing any results.

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Morgan. This morning I tested the draft online ballot platform and found a critical privacy issue. The platform records each voter's identity for 90 days, and there is no way to disable that record. This means the online ballot cannot guarantee anonymous voting — it fundamentally conflicts with what Ms. Ellis just described as required by our student-privacy protocol. Given this, I recommend we abandon the online ballot entirely and instead use sealed paper ballots counted by two adults, which would create zero electronic voter records and ensure the fully anonymous voting Ms. Ellis's safety review requires. I have not yet updated the election plan to reflect this workaround, so the current draft still references the online ballot.
